requirementChecks.criteria: Read the original file properties: Format: presentation document; at least eight actual pages. Stage: final.

The sheet occupies one page and records every handbook page assignment, the leaf key, common/scientific-name index and season finder, and all required species fields. It specifies the closed trim, two-column grid with margins and gutter, 140 gsm uncoated paper and saddle stitching. It names actual typefaces for body and navigation/caption use; generic categories alone are insufficient. Omitted assignments, routes, fields or specifications fail.

The handbook contains exactly 12 pages in reading order: front cover 1; how-to 2; key 3; Horse chestnut 4; Rowan 5; Norway maple 6; English oak 7; Silver birch 8; Beech 9; indexes and season finder 10; sources and credits 11; comparison/back cover 12. The rules and presentation describe this same allocation and explicitly state the six specified trim, page-count, spine and grid values. Supporting process or presentation pages must not be counted as handbook pages. The assembled book must retain the required cover strings, observation wording on pages 2 and 4–9, and comparison scale label on page 12.

The image visibly presents both a closed front cover and an open species spread in a reader's hand. Multiple views within the image are acceptable. Readable captions give 105 × 148 mm, 12 pages and saddle stitching. A missing view, missing hand-held presentation or an incorrect or omitted caption value fails.

The map and key distinguish complete compound leaves from individual leaflets and provide six traceable two-feature routes: radiating leaflets plus prickly conker case to Horse chestnut 4; paired leaflets along an axis plus fruit cluster to Rowan 5; sharply pointed lobes plus almost horizontal paired winged fruit to Norway maple 6; rounded lobes plus stalked acorns to English oak 7; triangular toothed leaf plus catkin or winged seed to Silver birch 8; pointed oval wavy-edged leaf plus prickly husk or triangular nut to Beech 9. Missing or conflicting evidence reaches the exact fallback label and page 2. How-to text explains that seasonal absence of flowers or fruit does not establish a tree's absence. Page 10 supplies alphabetically ordered common-name and modern scientific-name indexes with correct destinations, plus spring, summer, autumn and winter cues matching the supplied season records, including possible winter persistence of Norway maple fruit. Alternative diagram arrangements are acceptable; skipped corroboration, wrong destinations or unsupported seasonal claims fail.

Pages 2–3 retain the complete-leaf versus leaflet explanation, all six correctly paired leaf/second-feature routes, destinations 4–9 and the exact insufficient-evidence branch leading to page 2. The how-to preserves the seasonal-absence explanation. Page 10 retains both alphabetical name indexes and the supplied season finder: spring leaves and birch catkins; summer leaves and late-summer Rowan fruit; autumn conkers, Rowan fruit, oak acorns and Beech nuts; possible winter maple fruit. Missing material during assembly, changed destinations or contradictions with the delivered retrieval pages fail.

The three complete spreads pair b1/Horse chestnut/Aesculus hippocastanum with page 4, b2/Rowan/Sorbus aucuparia with 5, b3/Norway maple/Acer platanoides with 6, b4/English oak/Quercus robur with 7, b5/Silver birch/Betula pendula with 8 and b6/Beech/Fagus sylvatica with 9. Each entry includes its supplied leaf description, corroborating feature, observation-season note and source ID without changing their meaning. Each has at least two visible leader lines, covering its recorded leaf detail and second feature. A complete identifiable leaf or compound-leaf arrangement and the corroborating feature remain visible. Compare imagery with its corresponding supplied plate: colour, orientation, proportions, shapes, depicted part counts and organ attachments must remain intact. Uniform scaling, rectangular cropping and repeated details from the same plate are acceptable when required features survive. Wrong plates, historical names substituted for modern headings, lost diagnostic details or invented botanical parts fail.

Pages 4–9 preserve the six delivered species entries in order, including their plate/source assignments, common and modern scientific names, leaf and second-feature descriptions, season notes, page numbers and at least two feature-callout labels per entry. Check all six records, including Quercus robur, Betula pendula and Fagus sylvatica as modern headings despite different historical plate lettering. Omitted fields, incorrect seasonal claims or content changed during assembly fail.

Every front-cover depiction carries the exact title and subtitle. The thumbnail study identifies a 25 mm cover width and presents the cover at that intended viewing scale; both strings must remain decipherable there without relying on an enlarged companion view or transcription outside the cover. Missing copy, inconsistent wording or illegibility at the demonstrated scale fails. No exact raster dimension is required.

Read the complete observation phrase on page 2 and separately on each of pages 4, 5, 6, 7, 8 and 9. Its spelling, case and em dash match the fixed wording. One occurrence shared by a two-page species spread does not satisfy both pages; an occurrence only on page 3 does not satisfy page 2.

Both versions of page 12 provide a readable comparison of all six species, showing each recorded leaf structure or shape and its corroborating feature. References resolve to Horse chestnut 4, Rowan 5, Norway maple 6, English oak 7, Silver birch 8 and Beech 9. The exact relative-size label accompanies the plate comparison. Arrangement may vary only insofar as the standalone page and exterior still reproduce the same back-cover content; missing species, wrong features, wrong destinations or misleading relative scale fails.

Page 11 credits Otto Wilhelm Thomé's Flora von Deutschland, Österreich und der Schweiz, 1885, Gera, and scan distribution through Wikimedia Commons / biolib.de. Six individually matched records retain b1–b6, their modern scientific names, complete supplied Commons URLs and individual credit distinctions: Walther Otto Müller for b1; Walter Müller for b2; Walter Müller as lithographer for b3; W. Müller signatures for b4 and b6; no asserted individual artist for b5. Forestry England and Keele University Arboretum appear as factual sources. Historical illustrations are credited separately from present-day handbook text and design. Publication information includes First edition, 2026, PARK LEAVES imprint, the supplied handbook design credit and the copyright line for new text and layout. Compact formatting is acceptable; missing records, substituted URLs, invented attribution or treating historical plates as new handbook artwork fails.

Page 11 retains the complete six-record source register from the delivered spread: IDs, modern names, original Commons URLs and supplied individual image credits, plus the 1885 Thomé volume and scan distribution. It names both factual-source organisations and preserves the first-edition year, imprint, handbook design credit and new-text/layout copyright information. Historical illustration and current handbook authorship remain distinct. Lost URLs, missing records, incorrect attribution or omitted publication details fail.

Review the entire video and its duration. It lasts 10 seconds and visibly follows the key's rounded-lobe decision, corroboration by stalked acorns, the English oak entry on page 7, and comparison on page 12, in that sequence. Transitions and camera treatment may vary. Missing or reordered stages, unreadable destinations, a different species route or a different duration fails.
requirementChecks.manualReason: Inspect complete SHA-bound original outputs. This source draft contains no completed professional or model-output review; partial-frame/page sampling cannot prove whole-output compliance.

requirementChecks.criteria: The presentation has at least eight pages and visibly reuses every listed source deliverable. Legible scaling, crops and explanatory annotations are acceptable if the reused content remains recognisable and sufficient to assess it; filenames or textual claims alone do not count. It demonstrates rounded leaf lobes, stalked acorns, English oak page 7 and comparison page 12 in that order. Missing source coverage, substituted redesigns or a different route fails.

A readable production summary records 300 copies, four-colour digital printing, 140 gsm uncoated paper throughout, saddle stitching, 12 pages including covers, 105 × 148 mm closed trim, 210 × 148 mm exterior trim, a folded edge with 0 mm allocated spine panel, 3 mm exterior bleed, and the two-column grid with 8 mm margins and 4 mm gutter. Wording and units may be equivalently formatted. Missing or contradictory production values fail.

The flat exterior contains the complete front page 1 and comparison back page 12 positioned to form the booklet cover around a central folded edge. It identifies or depicts 3 mm bleed on the outside edges and has no allocated spine strip. Exterior wording occupies the front and back panels. Production annotations may explain trim, fold and bleed; exact pixel measurements are not assessed. Missing panels, an incorrect folding arrangement, absent bleed evidence or wording placed on an invented spine fails.

Page 12 retains a lower-right area reserved for the stated 30 × 20 mm ISBN barcode allocation, supported by an annotation or the page's physical-scale layout. The reserved area must not be occupied by comparison content. ISBN allocation remains pending, so a blank reservation or clearly identified placeholder is acceptable; a purported assigned ISBN is not. Judge the production allocation rather than exact raster dimensions.

Handbook body copy uses a serif face consistent with the actual typeface identified in the rules sheet. Specification evidence and the nominal page scale must support body text of at least 9.5 pt. Larger text is allowed. Sans-serif body copy, a smaller specified body size or visibly inconsistent use fails; exact font size must not be inferred from raw pixel counts alone.

Handbook navigation and captions use a sans-serif face matching the named specification, at a supported size of at least 8.5 pt. Larger text is allowed. Apply this requirement to added handbook typography, not retained historical lettering inside plates. Incorrect category, a smaller specified size or conflicting implementation fails; raw raster dimensions alone are not font-size evidence.

Each of the six pages presents the specified fields in the stated reading order, with the common name as its running header. The source ID sits at the outer edge above the page number, and the observation phrase spans the lower text area. Line wrapping and column flow may vary while preserving that hierarchy. Missing fields, reordered information or footer elements placed contrary to the record fail.

Record that proportional resizing, rectangular crops and repeated source-plate details are permitted treatments and do not themselves indicate altered botanical identity. This diagnostic does not fail files; required visible features and prohibited botanical changes are assessed by the plate-fidelity check.

The handbook layouts implement the rules sheet's named typefaces and page assignments without contradictory specifications. Handbook pages use the specified two-column grid, 8 mm margins and 4 mm gutter; judge the layout and stated physical specifications rather than exact raster dimensions. The six species pages share the prescribed field hierarchy, running-header convention and footer placement.

The thumbnail and closed portable cover reproduce the front cover in the exterior, allowing scale and perspective changes while preserving typography, imagery and copy. The portable open view reproduces one of the delivered species spreads with the same species pairing, page destinations and layout, allowing hand occlusion and perspective. The standalone comparison page and the exterior's back panel depict the same page 12, including six-entry content, scale label and barcode reservation.
